settings.narrowTip: The pane is too narrow, so the settings are collapsed. Widen the window to see them.

llm.title: LLM config
llm.desc: Manage model providers and models: endpoint, API key, context length and generation parameters.

mcp.title: MCP connections (outbound)
mcp.desc: Connect out to external MCP services as a client so agents can call their tools.

rpc.title: RPC connections (outbound)
rpc.desc: Connect out to external RPC services as a client so agents can call their APIs.

mcpserverconfig.title: MCP auth (inbound)
mcpserverconfig.desc: Choose how this tenant's MCP service authenticates incoming calls (API key / OAuth).

rpcserverconfig.title: RPC auth (inbound)
rpcserverconfig.desc: Choose how this tenant's RPC service authenticates incoming calls (API key / OAuth).

svcauthbindings.title: Service credentials
svcauthbindings.desc: Bind API keys / OAuth identities to tenant users; MCP and RPC share the same credentials.

users.title: Users
users.desc: Maintain tenant accounts, roles, passwords and per-user session / storage quotas.

globalVars.title: Global variables
globalVars.desc: Tenant-wide key/value config for workflows / agents / skills; exporting an asset carries the reference name, never the value.

tenantQuota.title: Tenant quota
tenantQuota.desc: Set this tenant's resource limits (agents / skills / workflows / session storage / sessions), bounded by the platform cap.

flowConfig.title: Workflow run limits
flowConfig.desc: Limit a workflow's run time, recursion depth, node count and record count (empty falls back to the system level).

agentConfig.title: Agent run limits
agentConfig.desc: Limit an agent's iterations, call depth, tool count and output size (empty falls back to the system level).

settings.flowHint: Tenant config: empty = fall back to the system level, -1 = unlimited; a tenant max_* cannot exceed the system level
settings.agentHint: Tenant config: empty = fall back to the system level; this group has no -1 (all four are safety valves, and "unlimited" removes the guard); tenant values cannot exceed the system level

max_timeout.label: Max timeout (s)
max_timeout.desc: Total run-time limit for a single run; it is terminated when reached

max_recursion_depth.label: Max recursion depth
max_recursion_depth.desc: How many levels deep workflows may call each other

max_node_count.label: Max nodes
max_node_count.desc: Number of nodes allowed in one flow graph

max_exec_count.label: Max executions
max_exec_count.desc: Cumulative node executions in a single run

max_run_records.label: Max run records
max_run_records.desc: How many historical runs are kept per workflow

max_session_records.label: Max session memory
max_session_records.desc: How many context records are kept in a session

max_iterations.label: Max iterations
max_iterations.desc: Max rounds of think → call tool → think in one conversation

max_call_depth.label: Max call depth
max_call_depth.desc: How deeply agents may call each other

max_tools.label: Max tools
max_tools.desc: How many tools a single agent may bind

max_output_bytes.label: Max output bytes
max_output_bytes.desc: Truncation length for a single command or tool output

max_agents.label: Max agents
max_agents.desc: How many agents this tenant may create

max_skills.label: Max skills
max_skills.desc: How many skills this tenant may create

max_flows.label: Max workflows
max_flows.desc: How many workflows this tenant may create

max_session_storage_bytes.label: Max session storage (tenant default)
max_session_storage_bytes.desc: Storage limit for one session workspace (MiB)

max_user_sessions.label: Max sessions per user (tenant default)
max_user_sessions.desc: How many sessions each user may own by default

sessions.title: Max sessions per user (user override)
sessions.hint: Session cap set for one user (empty follows the tenant, -1 = unlimited)

storage.title: Max session storage (user override)
storage.hint: Storage cap set for one user (empty follows the tenant, -1 = unlimited)

quota.intro: This tenant's default resource limits, bounded by the platform
quota.intro2: . When a per-user quota in Users is set to follow the tenant, it uses the effective values shown below.

quota.tip2: . Storage is in MiB and takes effect as soon as you save.
quota.invalidInt: Quotas must be integers (-1 = unlimited, empty = fall back to the system cap)

configTable.mustBePositive: {field} must be >= 1 (this group does not support -1 for unlimited)
configTable.saveFailedRetry: Failed to save, please try again later

globalVars.scopeTip: Global = tenant-wide, never shared across tenants
globalVars.usageTip: In a workflow: add an entry to the node's input variables, set the source to "Global variable", and reference it in the template as {input}; in agent / skill docs write {globalRef}. Asset packs carry the reference name only, never the value, so fill it in once after importing into another tenant.
globalVars.empty: No global variables yet. Create one from the top right, then set the source of a workflow node's input variable to "Global variable".
globalVars.namePlaceholder: e.g. DB_HOST (letters / digits / underscores, cannot start with a digit)
globalVars.secretKeepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current value
globalVars.secretHint: Secrets are read only at run time and never echoed back by the API; do not write them into AGENT.md / SKILL.md (they would land in the model context and run records).
globalVars.descPlaceholder: What this variable is for (carried with the asset pack's requirements list)
globalVars.templateHint: Node input variable: source_type = global, source_key = {name}; in the template write {input}
globalVars.invalidName: The name may only contain letters, digits and underscores, and cannot start with a digit
globalVars.invalidNumber: A number variable can only hold a number
globalVars.usageFailed: Failed to check references: {msg} (the server will check again on delete)
globalVars.confirmInUse: "{name}" is still referenced by: {where}{more}. Those places will fail at run time after deletion. Delete anyway?
globalVars.confirmUnused: Delete the global variable "{name}"? Workflows / agents referencing it will fail at run time (values are never silently empty).

users.introRoleManageRest: = can sign in to the console and use the backend;
users.introRoleServiceRest: = cannot sign in, it only acts as an API identity (bind it to an API key / OAuth under Service credentials). Disabling the account blocks both sign-in and API calls.
users.introQuota: When a quota follows the tenant, the effective value from Tenant quota applies; a custom value applies to this user only and cannot exceed the tenant cap.
users.primaryNoEditHint: primary is the root account created with the tenant and cannot be modified
users.primaryQuotaHint: primary's quota can only be changed by the platform
users.primaryDisableHint: primary is the root account and cannot be disabled
users.quotaActionHint: Set a quota for this user only
users.loginLabel: Login name (cannot be changed after creation)
users.roleManageRadio: Management user (can sign in to the console)
users.roleServiceRadio: Service user (cannot sign in, API identity only)
users.serviceUserTip: Service users have no password (so they cannot "suddenly gain" sign-in ability if switched to management later); the server handles the password automatically when the role changes.
users.quotaHint: Cannot exceed the tenant cap: sessions {sessions} / storage {storage}. Leaving a field empty makes it follow the tenant; 0 means the user cannot create sessions or write files.
users.primaryNoEdit: primary is the root account created with the tenant and cannot be modified
users.primaryQuotaOnly: primary is the root account created with the tenant, its quota can only be changed by the platform
users.primaryNoToggle: primary is the root account created with the tenant and cannot be disabled/enabled
users.customAtLeastOne: In custom mode fill at least one field, or switch back to Follow tenant default
users.managePwdMin: A management user password needs at least 8 characters
users.pwdMin: The password needs at least 8 characters

connection.namePlaceholder: Identifier used by programs only, letters and digits, e.g. weather123
connection.displayNamePlaceholder: Shown in the UI, may contain any language; empty means the connection id
connection.commandPlaceholder: Command to run, e.g. npx or python
connection.workDirPlaceholder: Working directory of the child process (optional, e.g. C:\app or /opt/app); defaults to the service process directory
connection.envHint2: and appended to the service process environment. Local credentials (such as API keys) belong here; stdio does not use auth.
connection.refreshToolsFailed: Failed to refresh the tool list: {msg}

bindings.tipIntro: Bind API key / OAuth identities to tenant users; MCP and RPC services share them.
bindings.tipCreate: This is the only place to create an API key: a new binding is restricted by default with no targets, so tick the allowed agents / workflows under Configure, otherwise the key cannot reach any endpoint.
bindings.scopeRestrictedEmpty: ⚠ Restricted but no target selected (cannot call any endpoint)
bindings.supervisorWarn: Once granted, an external credential can use tenant management abilities (create / modify / delete agents and skills, change grants). Review them one by one instead of selecting all.
bindings.pickerEmpty: No agent / workflow has an exposed endpoint
bindings.tipExclude1: This credential can call every exposed endpoint
bindings.tipExclude2: — newly exposed regular endpoints apply automatically, no need to update a whitelist; the supervisor's endpoints are the tenant management entry, so they are blocked here.
bindings.tipSelected1: Only the targets ticked in the left list are allowed. New bindings default to
bindings.tipSelected2: — forgetting to configure means it cannot call anything rather than everything.
bindings.emptyHintRestrict: No target selected — after saving this credential cannot call any endpoint
bindings.emptyHintExclude: Current scope: all endpoints except the supervisor (no need to pick them one by one)
bindings.emptyHintAll: Currently unrestricted: every exposed endpoint can be called
bindings.pickHint: Click Pick targets and tick items in the left list; ticking one target allows both its rpc and mcp endpoints. Select all regular does not include the supervisor.
bindings.alertNoTarget1: Restriction is on but no target is selected: after saving this credential will
bindings.alertNoTargetBold: be unable to call any endpoint
bindings.alertCandidates1: The list only contains agents / workflows
bindings.alertCandidates2: ; granting an internal-only target still cannot reach it.
bindings.addedApiKey: API key binding created: it is restricted by default with no target yet, click Configure to tick the allowed agents / workflows
bindings.addedOauth: OAuth binding created: it is restricted by default with no target yet, click Configure to tick the allowed agents / workflows
bindings.loadScopeFailed: Failed to load the endpoint scope: {msg}
bindings.savedRestrictedEmpty: Restriction enabled with no target: this credential cannot call any endpoint
bindings.savedExclude: Set to all endpoints except the supervisor
bindings.savedAll: Set to unrestricted: this credential can call every exposed endpoint
